```{r}

# ----------------------------
#Simulate ONE trial
# ----------------------------

set.seed(1)

# 1) Choose trial settings (assumptions)
n_per_group <- 200          # try 200 per arm for now
Delta <- 2                  # non-inferiority margin (PHQ-9 points)
sigma_followup <- 6.9       # SD of PHQ-9 at 12 weeks
rho <- 0.5                  # correlation between baseline and 12-week PHQ-9
alpha_one_sided <- 0.025    # one-sided alpha for non-inferiority

# 2) Generate treatment assignment
#    0 = Face-to-face CBT (control), 1 = Digital CBT (new)
treat <- rep(c(0, 1), each = n_per_group)

# 3) Simulate baseline PHQ-9 scores (roughly moderate depression)
#    We'll keep it simple: Normal with mean 15, SD 4
baseline <- rnorm(2 * n_per_group, mean = 15, sd = 4)

# 4) Create correlated noise so follow-up is related to baseline
#    If Z1 and Z2 are independent N(0,1),
#    then (rho*Z1 + sqrt(1-rho^2)*Z2) is N(0,1) and correlated with Z1 by rho
z1 <- scale(baseline)                 # standardized baseline ~ acts like Z1
z2 <- rnorm(2 * n_per_group)          # independent noise Z2
eps <- as.numeric(rho * z1 + sqrt(1 - rho^2) * z2)  # correlated N(0,1)

# 5) Simulate TRUE treatment effect (digital - face-to-face)
#    For planning, assume true difference is 0 (similar efficacy)
delta_true <- 0

# 6) Generate 12-week PHQ-9
#    Follow-up = (mean level) + (treatment effect) + (random variability)
#    We include a baseline relationship implicitly via eps construction.
mean_followup <- 9  # average PHQ-9 after treatment (plausible)
followup <- mean_followup + delta_true * treat + sigma_followup * eps

# 7) Run ANCOVA: follow-up ~ treatment + baseline
dat <- data.frame(followup = followup, treat = treat, baseline = baseline)

fit <- lm(followup ~ treat + baseline, data = dat)

# 8) Extract treatment effect estimate and its CI (digital - face-to-face)
#    In this model, the coefficient on treat is the adjusted mean difference
est <- coef(summary(fit))["treat", "Estimate"]
se  <- coef(summary(fit))["treat", "Std. Error"]

# For a one-sided alpha=0.025 NI test, we use the upper bound of the 95% two-sided CI
tcrit <- qt(1 - alpha_one_sided, df = fit$df.residual)  # ~97.5th percentile
upper_CI <- est + tcrit * se

# 9) Non-inferiority decision rule:
#    conclude NI if upper CI < Delta
non_inferior <- (upper_CI < Delta)

cat("Adjusted treatment effect estimate (digital - face-to-face):", round(est, 3), "\n")
cat("Upper CI bound:", round(upper_CI, 3), "\n")
cat("Non-inferior (upper CI < Delta)?", non_inferior, "\n")
```

```{r}
# ---------------------------------------------------
# Function that simulates ONE trial (ANCOVA)
# and returns TRUE/FALSE for non-inferiority success
# ---------------------------------------------------

one_trial_success <- function(n_per_group,
                              Delta = 2,
                              sigma_followup = 6.9,
                              rho = 0.5,
                              alpha_one_sided = 0.025,
                              delta_true = 0,
                              mean_baseline = 15,
                              sd_baseline = 4,
                              mean_followup = 9) {

  # Treatment assignment: 0=control (FtF), 1=digital (dCBT)
  treat <- rep(c(0, 1), each = n_per_group)

  # Baseline PHQ-9
  baseline <- rnorm(2 * n_per_group, mean = mean_baseline, sd = sd_baseline)

  # Correlated error term to induce baseline-followup correlation
  z1 <- scale(baseline)
  z2 <- rnorm(2 * n_per_group)
  eps <- as.numeric(rho * z1 + sqrt(1 - rho^2) * z2)

  # Follow-up PHQ-9 (12 weeks)
  followup <- mean_followup + delta_true * treat + sigma_followup * eps

  # ANCOVA
  dat <- data.frame(followup = followup, treat = treat, baseline = baseline)
  fit <- lm(followup ~ treat + baseline, data = dat)

  # Extract treatment effect and its SE
  est <- coef(summary(fit))["treat", "Estimate"]
  se  <- coef(summary(fit))["treat", "Std. Error"]

  # Upper bound for NI decision (upper 95% CI bound)
  tcrit <- qt(1 - alpha_one_sided, df = fit$df.residual)
  upper_CI <- est + tcrit * se

  # Non-inferiority success
  (upper_CI < Delta)
}

# Quick test: run ONE simulated trial and see TRUE/FALSE
set.seed(1)
one_trial_success(n_per_group = 200)
```
```{r}
# ---------------------------------------
#  Estimate power for a given n
# ---------------------------------------

estimate_power <- function(n_per_group, n_sims = 2000, seed = 123) {
  set.seed(seed)
  results <- replicate(n_sims, one_trial_success(n_per_group = n_per_group))
  mean(results)  # proportion of TRUE = estimated power
}

# power when n=200 per group
power_200 <- estimate_power(n_per_group = 200, n_sims = 2000, seed = 123)
power_200
```
```{r}
# -------------------------------------------------
# Search for minimum n with power >= 0.90
# -------------------------------------------------

target_power <- 0.90
n_values <- seq(120, 260, by = 10)   # try a range of sample sizes
power_results <- numeric(length(n_values))

for (i in seq_along(n_values)) {
  power_results[i] <- estimate_power(n_per_group = n_values[i],
                                      n_sims = 2000,
                                      seed = 123)
  cat("n =", n_values[i], 
      " -> Power =", round(power_results[i], 3), "\n")
}

# Combine results
results_table <- data.frame(
  n_per_group = n_values,
  power = power_results
)

results_table
```
